1	"""Single-file SQL query layer.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
6	  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
7	* :func:`query_files` -- run a statement against a table-name to path
8	  mapping, optionally chaining several equi-joins
9	* :func:`explain_file` / :func:`explain_files` -- parse, bind and plan the
10	  same statements without executing them; only file metadata is read
11	* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
12	* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
13	  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use
14	
15	The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::
16	
17	    query       := SELECT [DISTINCT] select_item (',' select_item)*
18	                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
19	                   [HAVING expr]
20	                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
21	                   [LIMIT uint]
22	    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' [DISTINCT] ('*' | ident) ')'
23	                   | scalar_expr AS alias
24	    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' [DISTINCT] ('*' | ident) ')')
25	                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
26	    expr       := or_expr
27	    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
28	    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
29	    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
30	    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
31	    postfix     := scalar_expr (IS [NOT] NULL)?
32	    scalar_expr := term (('+' | '-') term)*
33	    term        := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
34	    factor      := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
35	    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
36	                | CASE WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr
37	                  (WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr)*
38	                  (ELSE scalar_expr)? END
39	    operand     := ident | literal
40	    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
41	                   | single-quoted utf8
42	
43	The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
44	``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Each of
45	``COUNT`` / ``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` also accepts
46	``DISTINCT`` before its single column argument (``COUNT(DISTINCT ident)``
47	etc.): rows are first selected by WHERE, then within each group (or the
48	single global group) NULL arguments are ignored and the remaining values
49	are deduplicated by the column's type -- float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0``
50	count as the same value -- before the aggregate runs.  ``COUNT(DISTINCT
51	x)`` returns the number of distinct non-NULL values (0 on empty input,
52	a non-nullable int64); the other DISTINCT aggregates return NULL when no
53	distinct non-NULL value remains and otherwise keep the result type,
54	nullability, comparison rules and overflow / non-finite
55	:class:`QueryValidationError` behaviour of their plain counterparts.
56	DISTINCT here only deduplicates the aggregate's argument values; it does
57	not change ``SELECT DISTINCT`` row deduplication, and the argument stays
58	a single column reference (no ``*``, expressions, multiple arguments or
59	nested aggregates).  A misplaced DISTINCT keyword, a missing argument,
60	``*``, an expression or multiple arguments inside a DISTINCT call raise
61	:class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is opened.  DISTINCT
62	aggregates may appear wherever plain aggregates may (SELECT, HAVING,
63	ORDER BY), and textually identical calls share one computation.  Without
64	GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
65	GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
66	must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
67	allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported
68	for bare columns or aggregate calls.
69	
70	Scalar arithmetic (parentheses, unary ``+``/``-``, binary ``+`` ``-``
71	``*`` ``/``; precedence: parentheses, unary, ``*``/``/``, ``+``/``-``)
72	is available over int64 / float64 columns and numeric literals in SELECT
73	and WHERE.  A computed SELECT expression must be named with ``AS`` (the
74	alias follows the usual identifier rules and must be unique among the
75	output names); bare columns and aggregate calls keep their existing
76	result names.  int64 ``+``/``-``/``*`` on two int64 operands yields
77	int64; any float64 operand or a division yields float64, and unary
78	operators preserve the operand type.  Any NULL operand makes the result
79	NULL; the output column is nullable iff a participating column is
80	nullable (pure constants are not).  int64 overflow, division by zero and
81	non-finite float64 results raise :class:`QueryValidationError`.  A
82	numeric expression used directly as a boolean condition is rejected with
83	:class:`QueryValidationError` as well.  Non-aggregate queries execute
84	WHERE, then compute the sort keys, stably sort, apply LIMIT and only
85	then evaluate the SELECT expressions, so filtered or truncated rows
86	never trigger division-by-zero or overflow in the projection; a
87	DISTINCT query instead evaluates the projection right after WHERE,
88	deduplicates the result rows, and only then sorts and applies LIMIT.  ORDER BY
89	may name a SELECT alias (an alias shadows an input column of the same
90	name) and sorts on the expression's result type with the usual NULL
91	placement and stability rules.  Aggregate queries do not accept scalar
92	expressions: GROUP BY keys and aggregate arguments stay plain column
93	references, and mixing a scalar expression into an aggregate query
94	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
95	
96	``SELECT DISTINCT`` removes duplicate rows from a non-aggregate query:
97	the projection may be a star, plain columns or ``AS``-aliased scalar
98	expressions exactly as without DISTINCT, and deduplication compares the
99	full projected result row column by column after WHERE.  Two NULLs in
100	the same result column compare equal, NULL never equals a non-NULL
101	value, bool / utf8 / numeric values keep their existing comparison
102	semantics, and float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0`` compare equal.  Without
103	ORDER BY the surviving rows keep the order of the first occurrence of
104	each distinct result row; ORDER BY then sorts the deduplicated rows and
105	LIMIT keeps the first N.  The projection expressions are evaluated
106	only for rows that passed WHERE (and, with ORDER BY, before the sort),
107	so a division by zero, int64 overflow or non-finite float64 result that
108	actually occurs still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.  ORDER BY
109	of a DISTINCT query may name only bare columns or explicit aliases that
110	are part of the projection; an unprojected or otherwise unknown name
111	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`, and the sort direction, NULL
112	placement and stability rules are unchanged.  DISTINCT combined with
113	GROUP BY, HAVING or any aggregate projection raises
114	:class:`QueryValidationError`; argument-level ``DISTINCT`` inside an
115	aggregate call (``COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`` etc.) is a separate feature
116	described above and stays an aggregate query.  A missing projection, a
117	repeated DISTINCT or a misplaced DISTINCT keyword raises
118	:class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is opened.
119	
120	Searched CASE expressions
121	(``CASE WHEN cond THEN result [WHEN ...] [ELSE result] END``; the simple
122	``CASE value WHEN ...`` form is not supported and at least one WHEN is
123	required) are scalar operands and may be nested inside more arithmetic,
124	comparisons and other CASE expressions.  For each row the WHEN conditions
125	are tested in written order and only TRUE matches; FALSE and UNKNOWN fall
126	through, an explicit ELSE supplies the fallback and a missing ELSE yields
127	NULL.  Only the chosen result is evaluated, so division by zero, int64
128	overflow or a non-finite float64 inside an unhit branch never raises; a
129	chosen result that errors still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
130	Every reachable THEN and an explicit ELSE must share one type family:
131	int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64, while bool and utf8 must
132	match each other exactly (any other mix raises
133	:class:`QueryValidationError`).  The result column is nullable if any
134	reachable result is nullable or the ELSE is omitted.  WHEN conditions use
135	the same boolean type check and three-valued logic as WHERE; CASE stays a
136	scalar expression, so it is rejected in aggregate arguments, GROUP BY and
137	the projection of an aggregate query just like the other scalar
138	expressions.
139	
140	Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
141	NULL is a postfix of its scalar operand.  Comparison operands may be
142	column references, literals or scalar arithmetic expressions.  WHERE
143	follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
144	comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
145	logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.
146	
147	After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
148	its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
149	of their first selected row.  An optional HAVING clause between GROUP BY
150	and ORDER BY filters the formed groups with the same boolean expression
151	grammar and three-valued logic as WHERE: its conditions combine grouping
152	columns, aggregate calls and type-compatible literals with NOT / AND / OR
153	/ comparisons / IS [NOT] NULL, only groups whose condition is TRUE are
154	kept, and aggregates named in HAVING need not appear in SELECT.  Without
155	GROUP BY HAVING filters the single global aggregate row (still produced
156	when WHERE selected no rows); with GROUP BY an empty selection yields
157	zero groups.  HAVING may not name ungrouped plain columns, ``*``, CASE,
158	scalar arithmetic or nested aggregates; it is rejected on a completely
159	non-aggregate query.  ORDER BY may only name a selected result; ASC is the
160	default, NULLs sort last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST /
161	NULLS LAST is given, and groups equal on every sort key keep that
162	first-row order.  LIMIT then keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY
163	and aggregates an aggregate query over zero selected rows still yields one
164	output row (COUNT 0, the other aggregates NULL), unless HAVING removes it;
165	with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.
166	
167	Multi-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add a deterministic chain of zero
168	or more equi-joins to the grammar::
169	
170	    query := SELECT ... FROM from_table
171	             { join_kind JOIN next_table
172	               ON (earlier_table.col = next_table.col
173	                   | next_table.col = earlier_table.col) } ...
174	    join_kind := INNER | LEFT | RIGHT | FULL OUTER
175	
176	``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
177	the statement are read.  Each join step introduces exactly one not-yet-used
178	table (aliases and repeated tables are rejected) and its single ON equality
179	connects a qualified column of that new table with a qualified column of any
180	table introduced earlier (FROM or a previous join); the two sides of the
181	equality are interchangeable.  Compound or non-equality ON conditions,
182	other join types and ``FULL`` without ``OUTER`` are syntax errors raised
183	before any file is opened.  In any statement that contains a JOIN every
184	column reference outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be qualified as ``table.column``
185	(either part may be a double-quoted identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the
186	referenced schemas in FROM/JOIN order with ``table.column`` names; explicit
187	projections keep their qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase
188	``FUNC(table.column)`` labels.
189	
190	Each step is evaluated with the materialised intermediate result as its
191	left input and the newly read table as its right input.  Join keys may
192	share a type or mix int64 with float64; NULL keys never match.  INNER JOIN
193	emits every matching combination, LEFT JOIN also emits unmatched left rows
194	with the right-side values set to NULL (the new table's result columns are
195	nullable), RIGHT JOIN emits all new-table rows in new-file order (one new
196	row's matches expand in intermediate/current row order) padding the whole
197	intermediate side with NULL (every earlier table's result columns become
198	nullable), and FULL OUTER JOIN emits the LEFT JOIN output and then appends
199	the unmatched new rows in new-file order (every result column is nullable).
200	INNER / LEFT / FULL expand in the current intermediate row order, with the
201	matching new rows in new-file order within one current row; RIGHT expands
202	in new-file row order with the matches in current row order.  Nullability
203	is derived per step: once a step makes an earlier table's columns
204	nullable, later steps keep them nullable.  WHERE / GROUP BY / HAVING /
205	projection / DISTINCT / stable sorting / LIMIT run only after the whole
206	chain has been built, with their usual semantics.
207	
208	The multi-file entry points (:func:`query_files`, :func:`explain_files`)
209	take an optional ``join_strategy`` of ``"hash"`` or ``"sort_merge"``; an
210	explicit strategy is applied to every join step.  Both strategies accept
211	the same statements and return identical column descriptions, values, NULL
212	placement and row order; they differ only in how matching right rows are
213	located (a right-key hash index versus sorting both sides on the key and
214	merging equal-key runs).  With the argument omitted the historical
215	default join path is used and the explain plan carries no strategy field;
216	with an explicit strategy every plan Join operator gains a ``strategy``
217	field of ``HASH`` or ``SORT_MERGE``.  A JOIN-less statement accepts either
218	strategy but gains no extra operator, and an invalid strategy raises
219	:class:`ValueError` before any source file is opened.
220	
221	The explain plan lists the referenced sources and their Scan operators in
222	FROM/JOIN order with ``required_columns`` attributed to each source, then
223	one Join operator per step in the same order, recording the step type and
224	the two normalised qualified keys (the earlier table on the left, the
225	freshly introduced table on the right).
226	
227	Row-group-partitioned (v2) files are read selectively: every query decodes
228	only the column blocks its plan actually references (a join chain
229	additionally reads each table's ON keys).  Single-file statements
230	(:func:`query_file` and JOIN-less :func:`query_files`) and multi-file
231	statements whose whole join chain is INNER push the AND-connected,
232	type-compatible comparisons and IS [NOT] NULL conditions of WHERE down to
233	the per-group statistics.  In a join chain only a top-level AND leaf that
234	references exactly one source (a qualified column of that source compared
235	to a type-compatible literal, on either side, or that column's IS [NOT]
236	NULL) is attributed to that source; each source's own leaves are combined
237	with AND independently.  A chain containing any LEFT / RIGHT / FULL OUTER
238	step performs no row-group pruning at all (an OUTER step can pad a source
239	with NULLs, so no group can be proven absent), v1 sources are always read
240	in full, and in a mixed v1/v2 all-INNER chain only the v2 sources are
241	pruned.
242	
243	A row group is skipped only when a source's statistics prove its pushed
244	leaves cannot all be TRUE at once for any of the group's rows; OR, NOT,
245	CASE, arithmetic, column-to-column or cross-source comparisons and
246	undecidable ranges are never pushed, and neither block nor replace the
247	eligible leaves next to them.  Surviving rows are still filtered row by
248	row with the full WHERE condition over the complete join result, so NULL
249	three-valued logic, duplicate key combinations, aggregates, DISTINCT,
250	ordering, LIMIT and the deterministic unordered row order are unchanged.
251	When every group is excluded the statement simply sees zero rows, so
252	empty results, ``COUNT(*)``, other global aggregates and HAVING keep
253	their usual semantics.  Both format versions return identical column
254	descriptions, values, row order, sorting, LIMIT, join and export results
255	for the same data and statement.  Only the blocks of the columns and row
256	groups actually selected are decompressed or decoded: a block belonging
257	to an excluded group is never read even when corrupt, while a corrupt
258	block of a selected group raises
259	:class:`~columnar_analytics.format.ColumnarFormatError`.
260	
261	In the explain plan a v2 Scan operator of an eligible statement
262	(single-source, or an all-INNER chain) carries, right after
263	``required_columns``, the fields ``row_groups_total``,
264	``row_groups_selected`` and ``pushed_condition`` (the leaves attributed
265	to that source combined, in SQL appearance order, as one condition tree
266	with qualified column names, or null when no leaf was pushed; with no
267	pushed leaf selected equals total).  v1 Scan operators and the Scan
268	operators of a chain containing an OUTER step keep their historical
269	shape; the reported counts always match the groups execution reads.
270	"""

353	def _validate_join_strategy(join_strategy: Any) -> str | None:
354	    """Validate the optional ``join_strategy`` argument.
355	
356	    Returns the canonical lowercase strategy name, or ``None`` when the
357	    caller did not request one.  Any other value (including a non-string)
358	    raises :class:`ValueError`; callers run this before opening any file.
359	    """
360	    if join_strategy is None:
361	        return None
362	    if not isinstance(join_strategy, str) or join_strategy not in _JOIN_STRATEGIES:
363	        allowed = ", ".join(sorted(_JOIN_STRATEGIES))
364	        raise ValueError(
365	            f"invalid join_strategy: {join_strategy!r}; expected one of {allowed}"
366	        )
367	    return join_strategy

383	@dataclass(frozen=True)
384	class _Token:
385	    kind: str  # one of: keyword, ident, number, string, op, star, eof
386	    value: Any
387	    text: str
388	
389	
390	_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
391	    r"""
392	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
393	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
394	    """,
395	    re.VERBOSE,
396	)
397	# Bare identifiers: Unicode letters/underscore first, then word characters.
398	_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)
399	
400	
401	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
402	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
403	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
404	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
405	    i = 0
406	    n = len(sql)
407	    while i < n:
408	        ch = sql[i]
409	        if ch.isspace():
410	            i += 1
411	            continue
412	        if ch == "*":
413	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
414	            i += 1
415	            continue
416	        if ch in ",()+-/":
417	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
418	            i += 1
419	            continue
420	        if ch in "=<>!":
421	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
422	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
423	                i += 2
424	                continue
425	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
426	                op = ch + "="
427	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
428	                i += 2
429	                continue
430	            if ch in "=<>":
431	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
432	                i += 1
433	                continue
434	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
435	        if ch == "'":
436	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
437	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
438	            i = new_i
439	            continue
440	        if ch == '"':
441	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
442	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
443	            i = new_i
444	            continue
445	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
446	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
447	            if match:
448	                text = match.group(0)
449	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
450	                i = match.end()
451	                continue
452	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
453	            # used by multi-table queries ("table.column").
454	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
455	            i += 1
456	            continue
457	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
458	        if match:
459	            text = match.group(0)
460	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
461	            i = match.end()
462	            continue
463	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
464	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
465	    return tokens
466	
467	
468	def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
469	    lowered = word.lower()
470	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
471	        if lowered == "true":
472	            return _Token("number", True, word)
473	        if lowered == "false":
474	            return _Token("number", False, word)
475	        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
476	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)
477	
478	
479	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
480	    parts: list[str] = []
481	    i = start + 1
482	    n = len(sql)
483	    while True:
484	        j = sql.find("'", i)
485	        if j == -1:
486	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
487	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
488	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
489	            parts.append("'")
490	            i = j + 2
491	            continue
492	        value = "".join(parts)
493	        try:
494	            value.encode("utf-8")
495	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
496	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
497	        return value, j + 1
498	
499	
500	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
501	    parts: list[str] = []
502	    i = start + 1
503	    n = len(sql)
504	    while True:
505	        j = sql.find('"', i)
506	        if j == -1:
507	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
508	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
509	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
510	            parts.append('"')
511	            i = j + 2
512	            continue
513	        value = "".join(parts)
514	        if not value:
515	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
516	        return value, j + 1
517	
518	
519	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
520	    try:
521	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
522	            value: int | float = float(text)
523	        else:
524	            value = int(text, 10)
525	    except ValueError:
526	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
527	    if isinstance(value, int):
528	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
529	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
530	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
531	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
532	        return value
533	    if not math.isfinite(value):
534	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
535	    return value

541	# Node tuples:
542	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
543	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
544	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
545	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- as parsed (+ - * /)
546	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node, type_name)   -- after binding
547	#   ("unary", operand, negate)                        -- as parsed
548	#   ("unary", operand, negate, type_name)             -- after binding
549	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)   -- as parsed
550	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None, type_name) -- after binding
551	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
552	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
553	#   ("not", operand)
554	#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
555	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
556	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary" nodes are value nodes.
557	#
558	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
559	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
560	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
561	#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression

584	@dataclass(frozen=True)
585	class _Join:
586	    """One equi-join step of a multi-table query.
587	
588	    A statement may chain several steps in FROM/JOIN order; each step takes
589	    the intermediate result built so far as its left input and one freshly
590	    introduced table as its right input.
591	    """
592

633	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):

642	        select = self._parse_select()

648	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:

693	    def _parse_join_clauses(self) -> list[_Join]:
694	        # Zero or more join clauses may follow FROM; each introduces exactly
695	        # one new table with a single equi-ON condition.  "right" / "full" /
696	        # "outer" stay ordinary identifiers away from this clause (they are
697	        # matched with _accept_word), so columns carrying those names keep
698	        # working outside join parsing.
699	        joins: list[_Join] = []
700	        while True:
701	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
702	                self._expect_keyword("join")
703	                joins.append(self._parse_join("inner"))
704	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
705	                self._expect_keyword("join")
706	                joins.append(self._parse_join("left"))
707	            elif self._accept_word("right"):
708	                self._expect_keyword("join")

710	            elif self._accept_word("full"):

712	                self._expect_word("outer")

751	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
752	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
753	        while self._accept_op(","):
754	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
755	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
756	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
757	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
758	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
759	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
760	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
761	        tok = self._peek()

763	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"

767	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
768	            )

770	                raise QueryValidationError(

772	                )

776	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
777	        tok = self._peek()

869	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
870	        tok = self._peek()

887	        self._expect_op(")")

889	            "agg",
890	            func=func.upper(),

892	            distinct=distinct,

897	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
898	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
899	        # table-qualified) identifier, optionally preceded by DISTINCT.
900	        # Returns (name, table, table_quoted, distinct); name "" stands
901	        # for '*'.  DISTINCT only deduplicates the argument values of this
902	        # call; it accepts a single column reference only, and any other
903	        # use (a star, a missing argument, an expression, extra arguments
904	        # or a nested call) is a syntax error raised before any file is
905	        # opened.
906	        tok = self._peek()
907	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
908	            raise QueryValidationError(
909	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
910	            )

912	            self._next()
913	            tok = self._peek()
914	            if tok.kind == "star":
915	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
916	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) does not accept '*'"
917	                )

919	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
920	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) requires one column argument, "
921	                    f"got {tok.text!r}"
922	                )

924	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
925	                name, table, table_quoted = item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted
926	            else:
927	                self._next()
928	                name, table, table_quoted = tok.value, None, False
929	            nxt = self._peek()
930	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
931	                raise QuerySyntaxError(

933	                    "not a function call"
934	                )
935	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
936	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
937	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column "
938	                    "reference, not an expression"
939	                )
940	            return (name, table, table_quoted, True)
941	        if tok.kind == "star":

946	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
947	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
948	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
949	            )
950	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
951	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
952	            nxt = self._peek()
953	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
954	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
955	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
956	                )

958	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted, False)
959	        self._next()
960	        nxt = self._peek()
961	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
962	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
963	                raise QueryValidationError(
964	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
965	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
966	                )
967	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
968	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
969	            )
970	        self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)

1160	    def _parse_or(self) -> tuple:
1161	        node = self._parse_and()
1162	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
1163	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_and())
1164	        return node
1165	
1166	    def _parse_and(self) -> tuple:
1167	        node = self._parse_comparison()
1168	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
1169	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_comparison())
1170	        return node

1172	    def _parse_comparison(self) -> tuple:
1173	        left = self._parse_not_factor()
1174	        tok = self._peek()
1175	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
1176	            self._next()
1177	            right = self._parse_not_factor()
1178	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
1179	        return left
1180	
1181	    def _parse_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
1182	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
1183	            return ("not", self._parse_not_factor())
1184	        return self._parse_postfix()
1185	
1186	    def _parse_postfix(self) -> tuple:
1187	        node = self._parse_arith()
1188	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
1189	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
1190	            self._expect_keyword("null")
1191	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)

1194	    # Arithmetic expressions (numeric scalar operands) ------------------------
1195	    # Precedence (highest first): parentheses, unary +/-, * /, + -.
1196	
1197	    def _parse_arith(self) -> tuple:
1198	        node = self._parse_term()
1199	        while True:
1200	            tok = self._peek()
1201	            if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
1202	                self._next()
1203	                node = ("arith", tok.value, node, self._parse_term())
1204	            else:
1205	                return node

1207	    def _parse_term(self) -> tuple:
1208	        node = self._parse_factor()
1209	        while True:
1210	            tok = self._peek()
1211	            if tok.kind == "star":
1212	                self._next()
1213	                node = ("arith", "*", node, self._parse_factor())
1214	            elif tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == "/":
1215	                self._next()
1216	                node = ("arith", "/", node, self._parse_factor())
1217	            else:
1218	                return node

1220	    def _parse_factor(self) -> tuple:
1221	        tok = self._peek()
1222	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
1223	            negate = tok.value == "-"
1224	            self._next()
1225	            nxt = self._peek()
1226	            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
1227	                # A signed numeric literal is folded at parse time so the
1228	                # signed int64 range check keeps its historical meaning
1229	                # (-9223372036854775808 is valid, the bare magnitude is not).
1230	                self._next()
1231	                value = nxt.value
1232	                if isinstance(value, int):
1233	                    if negate:
1234	                        value = -value
1235	                    if not (-(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1):
1236	                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
1237	                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
1238	                        )
1239	                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
1240	                if negate:
1241	                    value = -value
1242	                return ("literal", value, "float64")
1243	            if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident") and not (
1244	                nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "("
1245	            ) and not (nxt.kind == "keyword" and nxt.value == "case"):
1246	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
1247	                    "sign must be followed by a numeric literal or expression"
1248	                )
1249	            return ("unary", self._parse_factor(), negate)
1250	        node = self._parse_atom()
1251	        if (
1252	            node[0] == "literal"
1253	            and isinstance(node[1], int)
1254	            and not isinstance(node[1], bool)
1255	            and node[1] > 2**63 - 1
1256	        ):
1257	            # The magnitude 2**63 is only reachable through an explicit
1258	            # negation; a bare literal must fit the signed int64 range.
1259	            raise QuerySyntaxError("integer literal is outside the int64 range")
1260	        return node

1262	    def _parse_atom(self) -> tuple:
1263	        if self._accept_op("("):
1264	            node = self._parse_or()
1265	            self._expect_op(")")
1266	            return node
1267	        if self._accept_keyword("case"):
1268	            return self._parse_case()
1269	        tok = self._peek()
1270	        if tok.kind == "number":
1271	            self._next()
1272	            value = tok.value
1273	            if isinstance(value, bool):
1274	                return ("literal", value, "bool")
1275	            type_name = "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64"
1276	            return ("literal", value, type_name)
1277	        if tok.kind == "string":
1278	            self._next()
1279	            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
1280	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
1281	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
1282	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
1283	                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
1284	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
1285	            if (
1286	                tok.kind == "ident"
1287	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
1288	                and nxt.kind == "op"
1289	                and nxt.value == "("
1290	            ):
1291	                raise QueryValidationError(
1292	                    f"aggregate {tok.value.upper()}(...) is not allowed here"
1293	                )
1294	            self._next()
1295	            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
1296	        if tok.kind == "keyword":
1297	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in expression")
1298	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected token {tok.text!r} in expression")
1299	
1300	    def _parse_case(self) -> tuple:
1301	        # A searched CASE: at least one "WHEN cond THEN result", an optional
1302	        # "ELSE result", terminated by END.  Conditions are boolean
1303	        # expressions; results are scalar (numeric, bool or utf8) and may
1304	        # themselves contain nested CASE expressions.  The simple form
1305	        # (CASE value WHEN ...) is not supported.
1306	        branches: list[tuple] = []
1307	        while True:
1308	            self._expect_keyword("when")
1309	            condition = self._parse_or()
1310	            self._expect_keyword("then")
1311	            result = self._parse_arith()
1312	            branches.append((condition, result))
1313	            tok = self._peek()
1314	            if not (tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "when"):
1315	                break
1316	        else_node = None
1317	        if self._accept_keyword("else"):
1318	            else_node = self._parse_arith()
1319	        self._expect_keyword("end")
1320	        return ("case", tuple(branches), else_node)

1322	    # Token helpers -----------------------------------------------------------
1323	
1324	    def _peek(self) -> _Token:
1325	        return self.tokens[self.pos]
1326	
1327	    def _next(self) -> _Token:
1328	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
1329	        self.pos += 1
1330	        return tok
1331	
1332	    def _accept(self, kind: str) -> bool:
1333	        if self._peek().kind == kind:
1334	            self.pos += 1
1335	            return True
1336	        return False
1337	
1338	    def _accept_op(self, value: str) -> bool:
1339	        tok = self._peek()
1340	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == value:
1341	            self.pos += 1
1342	            return True
1343	        return False
1344	
1345	    def _accept_keyword(self, value: str) -> bool:
1346	        tok = self._peek()
1347	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == value:
1348	            self.pos += 1
1349	            return True
1350	        return False
1351	
1352	    def _accept_word(self, value: str) -> bool:
1353	        # Match a reserved word that is otherwise lexed as an ordinary
1354	        # (non-keyword) identifier; used for RIGHT / FULL / OUTER, which keep
1355	        # their meaning as column names outside the join clause.
1356	        tok = self._peek()
1357	        if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() == value:
1358	            self.pos += 1
1359	            return True
1360	        return False
1361	
1362	    def _expect_word(self, value: str) -> _Token:
1363	        tok = self._peek()
1364	        if tok.kind != "ident" or tok.value.lower() != value:
1365	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value.upper()}, got {tok.text!r}")
1366	        return self._next()
1367	
1368	    def _expect_keyword(self, value: str) -> _Token:
1369	        tok = self._peek()
1370	        if tok.kind != "keyword" or tok.value != value:
1371	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value.upper()}, got {tok.text!r}")
1372	        return self._next()
1373	
1374	    def _expect_op(self, value: str) -> _Token:
1375	        tok = self._peek()
1376	        if tok.kind != "op" or tok.value != value:
1377	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value!r}, got {tok.text!r}")
1378	        return self._next()

1579	    if select.star:
1580	        raise QueryValidationError("'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY")

1585	        and not select.has_aggregate

1598	    group_indices: list[int] = []

1613	    # projected.

1627	                _BoundItem(
1628	                    "agg",
1629	                    output_name=label,
1630	                    func=func,
1631	                    arg_index=arg_index,
1632	                    arg_type=arg_col.type if arg_col is not None else "",

1649	            )

1653	            )

1661	            if col_index not in group_index_set:
